VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`, bypassing the model's `before_validation` that strips `http://` and paths. Old code supported hosts stored with `http://` prefixes (per removed tests like 'works with a http host' in site_setting_spec.rb and `allows_embeddable_host?` stripping logic), and `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` matches only bare hostnames via `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, so migrated URL-prefixed rows would never match. This is verifiable from the diff and constitutes a real migration data

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the backfill inserts rows via raw SQL string interpolation: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. This bypasses `EmbeddableHost` model callbacks (`before_validation` strips `http(s)://` and paths) and its validations, so previously stored setting lines like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (as seen in updated specs) would be persisted with scheme/path. Later, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` against the bare hostname (e.g., `example.com`), which will not match rows stored as full URLs. This can break embedding for hosts migrated from the old setting.
